@copilot Update this PR directly to implement the user's request: "replace with takesArgumentsNamed". Replace the unreleased names(String...) iterable matcher with a method-level AgentElementMatchers.takesArgumentsNamed(String... names) helper. Preserve the existing draft state and base branch. Do not create another PR as a workaround or migrate additional instrumentations.

The replacement must match exact ordered erased parameter type names, including primitives such as "int" and empty signatures. Return a chainable ElementMatcher.Junction for MethodDescription, following the existing generic matcher factory conventions. Clone the supplied names array at construction. Remove the now-unused names(...) factory and NamesMatcher implementation introduced in this PR; these additions are unreleased, so this is not a published API deprecation.

Check method.getParameters().size() against the expected name count before accessing any parameter types. After the arity check, use the parameter list's asTypeList() view and indexed access to compare each erased type's getName(), returning false immediately at the first mismatch. Do not compose this through Byte Buddy's takesArguments(iterableMatcher) or collect the erased types into an intermediate list. A small dedicated method matcher is appropriate. The intended call site is named("query").and(takesArgumentsNamed("org.influxdb.dto.Query", "int", "java.util.function.Consumer")).

The reason for this change is verified against Byte Buddy 1.18.15: takesArguments(iterableMatcher) wraps the iterable matcher in CollectionErasureMatcher, which eagerly collects every actual erased parameter type in an ArrayList before invoking names(...). This loses the old arity-first rejection. Conversely, the old positional CollectionElementMatcher restarts an iterator for every index. The method-level helper should retain cheap arity rejection while avoiding repeated prefix traversal and the eager erased-type collection.

Change the same six complete async/chunked query signature matchers in instrumentation/influxdb-2.4/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/influxdb/v2_4/InfluxDbImplInstrumentation.java to use takesArgumentsNamed(...). Keep all expected parameter names, advice bindings, telemetry, lifecycle behavior, synchronous overload predicates, intentional partial signatures, enum checks, and other overload alternatives unchanged.

Update or rename the shared matcher tests in javaagent-tooling/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/tooling/bytebuddy/matcher/NamesMatcherTest.java for the new method-level API. Retain exact success, wrong type, ordering, too few and too many parameters, primitives, empty parameter lists, and generic erasure coverage. Add focused coverage proving wrong arity rejects before accessing parameter types and a type mismatch stops subsequent type extraction. Follow existing test conventions and use suitable lazy descriptions or mocks to verify those contracts without timing assertions or a benchmark suite. Update the public helper Javadoc to describe its current method-signature contract.

Read CONTRIBUTING.md and the applicable repository instructions. Run the narrowest relevant formatter and shared matcher tests plus applicable existing InfluxDB instrumentation tests and supported dependency variants where feasible. Record actual commands and outcomes in coding evidence, but do not wait for unrelated CI. Keep this change bounded to the helper, its tests, and the existing InfluxDB example migration; do not change the intended behavior merely to satisfy tests.

replies.body: Implemented and committed as `dc686acf`. The replacement matcher checks arity first, then compares erased parameter names by index and stops on the first mismatch. Only the six requested InfluxDB predicates were migrated; targeted tests and formatting passed.
